draft.title: Tense and the order of events
card: Events are told as happening now: "I open the door and step inside." This feels immediate, as if the reader is there as it happens.
Events are told as already finished: "I opened the door and stepped inside." This often feels reflective, as the narrator looks back.
A flashback jumps back to an earlier time, such as a scene from a character's childhood. It can explain why a character acts as they do.
A jump forward moves ahead to a later time. It can build suspense or let the reader know what will happen before the characters do.
draft.remember: Tense sets the feel of the story, and changing the order of events changes what the reader knows and when.

a.q: Which sentence is written in the present tense?
opts: Mina pushes open the creaking gate
Mina pushed open the creaking gate
Mina had pushed open the creaking gate
Mina will push open the creaking gate
a.why: Pushes tells the reader the action is happening now. Pushed and had pushed are past tense, and will push is a future form.
a.clue: Which verb describes the action as it happens?

b.q: A story about Leo's football final stops to show a scene from two years earlier, when he quit the team. What does this scene do?
opts: It is a flashback that explains why the final matters to him
It is a jump forward that shows how the match ends
It is present tense, so the match feels more immediate
It is a reflective ending that sums up the story
b.why: Going back to an earlier time is a flashback, and it gives the reader background on Leo's feelings. A jump forward moves ahead in time, not back.
b.clue: Is the scene earlier or later than the final?

a.best: Mina pushes open the creaking gate

b.best: It is a flashback that explains why the final matters to him
